adversarial_case_ref: packet 06-naga-claim-ledger.md, 'Golden set and adversarial cases': 'amended/repealed rules'
expected_behavior: The successor edge below must be independently re-derivable from claim_v2.supersedes_claim_ref alone (per 02-p04-adapter-mapping.md §3's 'belt and suspenders' note on D10/D11 absence) -- i.e. if the edge object were lost or never written, a correct implementation can reconstruct the same supersession fact by reading claim_v2 directly. A test should delete the edge object and confirm the claim-level field alone still lets a reader find the current claim from the superseded one's claim_family_id.

notes.claim_v1_original: SYNTHETIC -- original PMA paid-up capital rule, IDR 2.5B.
notes.claim_v2_amendment: SYNTHETIC -- an amending regulation, same value; a per-KBLI/per-location exception threshold is out of scope for this fixture. Regulation numbers and dates are invented.
notes.object_successor_edge: Successor + edge commit atomically, in one transaction (CONTRACTS.md:142, :267; RULING B1, R1 §5a).

correction_2026_08_26: CORRECTED per RULING Zero 2026-08-26 (Research OS B1): a claim's 'superseded' state is DERIVED AT READ from the successor edge and is NEVER written onto the predecessor -- 'il vecchio resta intatto'. A reader obtains 'superseded from 2026-05-15' from claim_v2.supersedes_claim_ref, which this fixture's own expected_behavior already requires to be independently re-derivable. RESIDUAL, disposed 2026-09-11 (R1 §5d, §B2): a predecessor's valid_to is NEVER written even when the amending instrument states an explicit cessation date -- see 07-open-questions-and-corrections.md §B2.
correction_2026_09_11_r1: REWRITTEN under R1 (mission R1, base 9304392d1a, R1-build-spec.md §5b): claim_v1_original and claim_v2_amendment are now FULL canonical Claim objects (evidence_refs/confidence/classification/review/lineage/retention/object_hash all populated, computed via research_os.hashing.object_hash, never hand-typed) so the fixture validates against claim.schema.json and object_successor_edge.schema.json. Previously claim_v2_amendment.supersedes_claim_ref.object_hash ('9999...') and object_successor_edge.predecessor_ref.object_hash ('7777...') were two DIFFERENT placeholder strings bound to the SAME predecessor claim -- both are now the same computed hash of claim_v1_original. The predecessor keeps status='supported' and valid_to=null unchanged (RULING B1).
